title: A Marketplace sale's copy in the business's books: written whole or not at all, the tenant put back after each write, and the portal's own connection refused
why: Gate 5 (decisions/0181 §1, money records; the IT Manager's (11) ticket from the session manager, 2026-11-27). MarketCheckout::writeOrder writes the sale into the business's walled data (decisions/0110) through BusinessData::open, which switched the whole request to that business (Scope::enterBusiness) and never switched back. On live, the daily tick's reconcile (MarketCheckout.php:756) marks several card orders paid in one request, and from the second on Scope.php:19 threw 'already working for a business': the business never got that order or its payment in Quotes & invoices. Placing a direct-pay order ran writeOrder outside any try (:391), so a failed copy reached the buyer as an error with no payment instructions though the order was placed. And a copy that failed after its first line was left half-written (a draft with part of the total, never linked). Now: BusinessData::scoped opens the business on its own connection, runs the write and, in a finally, sets @tv_tenant to NULL and leaves (Scope::leave, refused for any connection but the one that entered); a request already inside a business (the portal) is refused before anything is written. writeOrder writes the copy in one transaction (its lines, total and card payment, or nothing). place and markPaid catch a failed copy: the order keeps a note, our team gets one Work queue ticket per order, and the business is told where the order is meanwhile (E-commerce setup → Marketplace orders) and that our team adds the invoice (for a card order, with its payment, so they don't record it twice); the raw error goes only to the server's log. Such a direct-pay order's hold waits for its copy: the daily check doesn't expire it or release its dates or stock until our team has linked it (the CFO's condition), and the ticket names the hold's deadline. Not in this release (the CFO's (4) second pass, 2026-11-27): the system's own second try at a failed copy, and writing the copies live's older orders are missing, are their own release behind a switch, with the CFO's seven points (reuse only an approved copy, the order's own tax rate and payment date, a retry cap, expired orders, the duplicate-payment key, a stricter key than the title). MarketSquare::import and sync (MarketSquare.php:120, :160) also open a business and never leave: their own ticket. No data is changed by this release.

changes.what: Card orders marked paid together each reach their business's Quotes & invoices; a copy is written whole or not at all

A copy that can't be written: the business is told where the order is meanwhile and that our team adds the invoice; the team gets a Work queue ticket; the buyer of a direct-pay order still gets how to pay

checks.write-order: tools/market-tests/write-order.php 21 on MariaDB with the listings realm BusinessData::ensure builds (its triggers and views): two businesses in one request both written, each in its own; owner 0 and no business connection after; @tv_tenant NULL on the connection after and a write on it refused; a throw midway comes back with the scope at 0 and the next business still written; a portal request refused with why, nothing written, its scope and tenant untouched; Scope::leave refuses another connection; a copy failing after its first line leaves no invoice, line or customer and no link; a copy written whose link fails raises one ticket, never the business told it is missing. On the live code it fails at the second write; the first build fails the half-written checks.
checks.write-order-place: tools/market-tests/write-order-place.php 24 on MariaDB, MarketCheckout's place(), markPaid() and tick() as built with stand-ins for the outside libraries they pass through: a direct-pay order placed with its invoice and the usual words; a failed copy never the buyer's error, the buyer still told how to pay or sent the receipt, the business told where the order is and that our team adds it (a card order: don't record the payment yourself), never the raw error, one Work queue ticket per order naming the hold's deadline, nothing half-written, the scope at 0; the next business's order in the same request written; past its hold, an order whose copy failed stays waiting and one with its copy expires, and it expires once its copy is linked.
checks.reviews: The CFO's (4) Tier 4, three passes (approved on its hold condition, built), and an independent QA check, three passes (its last low finding, the note outside its try, fixed); their findings in the hand-off. Design approved the words.
